# Proposal: Executive Workshop for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel and Sponsor
**Program:** Executive Workshop, AI Governance Academy
**Basis:** Discovery call notes of 6 October 2026

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client's AI activity spans three stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The Client describes its AI maturity as Piloting. In June 2026 an internal audit finding recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. The regulatory drivers named are the EU AI Act and GDPR. ISO/IEC 42001 work is expected to start next year, although the start date is not fixed.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. Its stated constraints are:

- A budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

Your stated objective is clear: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." A decision is expected by 15 December 2026.

## 2. Why a One-Day Executive Session Fits Now

**Maturity.** At the Piloting stage the decisions that shape governance have not yet been locked in by production use. One of the three use cases is already deployed, one is in pilot and one is planned. That spread lets the leadership group set ownership, risk appetite and oversight once and apply them across all three stages, rather than retrofitting controls later.

**Timeline.** A decision by 15 December 2026 leaves a short window before the Q2 2027 production target for visual inspection. A single structured day produces the decisions and draft roadmap that the following months of work depend on. It does not require a long engagement before anything is agreed.

**Existing systems.** The Client holds an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 QMS. The Workshop positions AI governance as an extension of these systems rather than a parallel structure. The Profile Block does not state which registers, processes, controls or records within them would host AI governance. Specific attachment points are therefore `Unknown` and will be identified with the room.

## 3. Workshop Structure and Emphasis for Tamarack Instruments

The Workshop runs as one live virtual day of four 90-minute blocks with breaks. It draws on the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen).

| Block | Focus | Emphasis for the Client |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Alignment | Current AI posture and a shared statement of governance intent | The three use cases at their three stages and the June 2026 finding of no AI inventory. Intent is anchored to the Q2 2027 visual inspection objective. |
| 2. Principles | Governance operating principles, agreed and ranked by the room | The three Academy principles applied to the Client: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. EU data residency and works council consultation are treated as standing inputs. |
| 3. Roadmap | Draft 12-month roadmap with owners | Sequencing against the EU AI Act, GDPR and the ISO/IEC 42001 preparation expected next year, built as an extension of the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and ISO 9001 QMS. Responding to the inventory finding is a candidate early item. |
| 4. Decisions | Executive decision log | Governance ownership, risk appetite for AI, oversight cadence and a budget mandate considered against the stated approval of up to US$80,000. |

Block 4 closes with *The Turtle and the Phoenix* and the facilitation kit's twenty-minute closing exercise (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md). This slot is the retention device for the three principles.

Where board-level reporting or acceptance criteria arise, the session may reference AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) and The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done).

**Regulatory content.** Discussion of the EU AI Act and GDPR is orientation, not legal advice. Two items in particular should be confirmed with external counsel:

- The classification of the visual inspection use case under the EU AI Act.
- The GDPR implications of the chatbot and the planned forecasting.

## 4. Proposed Participants

The proposed participants are executive leadership, the General Counsel, the CISO, the Head of Quality, the Head of Data, the German plant manager and two internal auditors, as listed in the Profile Block.

Ownership of individual decisions and roadmap items is assigned in the room. It is not assumed in advance.

## 5. Deliverables

1. **Decision log:** records decisions on governance ownership, risk appetite for AI, oversight cadence and budget mandate. Each entry carries an owner, a rationale and a review date. Items touching the EU AI Act or GDPR are flagged for confirmation with external counsel.
2. **Prioritized roadmap:** a draft 12-month sequence of governance work with owners, aligned to the Q2 2027 objective and the ISO/IEC 42001 preparation.
3. **Readiness observations:** facilitator observations on current governance posture, drawn from the GRC Workbook domains. These are observations for leadership use. They are not an audit opinion, and they do not predict any certification or audit outcome.

## 7. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** one day, live virtual, four 90-minute blocks with breaks.
- **Price:** US$7,500. This sits within the Client's stated approved budget of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- **Pre-work:** a short participant packet, issued after the date is confirmed.

## 8. Next Step

Please confirm three things:

1. Your intent to proceed, ahead of the 15 December 2026 decision date.
2. A preferred workshop date.
3. The final participant list.

On confirmation we will issue the pre-work packet and work through the open items in Section 6 with your team.
